paper.title: Covariance-adapting algorithm for semi-bandits with application to sparse rewards

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic combinatorial semi-bandits with kappa^2-sub-Gaussian marginals and ||.||_1-sub-exponential distribution
unmapped: outcome vector is jointly distributed (correlated arms); joint sub-exponential assumption E[exp(lambda^T(X-mu))] <= exp(lambda^T Sigma* lambda) for ||lambda||_1 <= 1/(2 kappa), with unknown covariance Sigma*
sub-Gaussian constant kappa of marginals known (mapped to sigma)
settings.definition_quote:
\begin{assumption}[$\kappa^2$-sub-Gaussian marginals] There is a constant $\kappa>0$ (known to the agent) such that $\forall i \in [\arms], \forall \lambda \in \R,~\EE{e^{\lambda\pa{X_i-\mu^*_i}}}\leq e^{\kappa^2\lambda^2/2}.$\label{ass:compo_subgau}\end{assumption}
Assumption~\ref{ass:compo_subgau} is not difficult to satisfy, and does not require any precision on the correlations between outcomes.
In particular, Assumption~\ref{ass:compo_subgau} includes Gaussian outcomes (with variance lower than $\kappa^2$) and bounded outcomes (with $\norm{\bX}_\infty\leq \kappa$). 
We also assume that $\bX$ satisfies the following. 
% [printed: Assumption 2]
\begin{assumption}[$\norm{\cdot}_1$-sub-exponential distribution]
 $\forall\blambda\in \R^\arms$ such that $\norm{\blambda}_1\leq 1/\pa{2\kappa}$, we have $\EE{e^{\blambda\transpose\pa{\bX-\bmu^*}}}\leq e^{\blambda\transpose\bSigma^*\blambda}$, where $\bSigma^*\triangleq \EE{\pa{\bX-\bmu^*}\pa{\bX-\bmu^*}\transpose}$ is the covariance matrix of $\bX$.

algorithms.name: ESCB-C (Efficient Sampling for Combinatorial Bandits with Covariance estimate)

symbols.Sigma_LB: sum over arms i not in A* of max_{A in A, i in A} sum_{j in A} Sigma*_ij

conditions: consistent policy (R_T = o(T^a) for all a>0)
for any covariance matrix Sigma* >= 0 there exists an instance (disjoint actions of size m, Gaussian outcomes) with all gaps equal to Delta

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: For any $n,m\in \N^*$ such that $n/m\geq 2$ is an integer, any $n\times n$ matrix $\bSigma^*\succeq 0$, any $\Delta>0$, and any consistent policy, there exists an instance with $n$ arms ... on which the regret satisfies \[\liminf_{T\to \infty} \frac{\Delta}{\log\pa{T}}R_T\geq 2\sum_{i\in[n],~i\notin A^*}\max_{A\in \cA,~i\in A}\sum_{j\in A}\Sigma^*_{ij}\]

results.notes: Regret defined as E[sum Delta(A_t)], i.e. pseudo-regret. Worst-case instance construction for a given Sigma*.

bound.regime: Delta_min small enough: Delta v (Delta + Delta log(Delta_max/Delta))^{3/2} <= c (log(m+1) Sigma_UB / n^2)^{3/2}

symbols.Sigma_UB: sum over all arms i of max_{A in A, i in A} sum_{j in A} max(0, Sigma*_ij)

conditions: Assumptions 1 and 2 hold (kappa-sub-Gaussian marginals, ||.||_1 sub-exponential with covariance Sigma*)
Delta small enough relative to log(m+1) Sigma_UB / n^2 (universal constant c)

source.label: thm:upper_cov
source.quote: Assume that the outcome distribution $\Prb_{\bX}$ satisfies Assumptions~\ref{ass:subgau} and~\ref{ass:subexp} ... If $\Delta$ is small enough ... then the regret of Algorithm~\ref{algo:cov} is upper bounded as \[\limsup_{T\to \infty}\! \frac{\Delta}{\log T} R_T \leq c' \log^2(m+1)\!\sum_{i\in [\arms]}\max_{A\in \actions,i\in A}\sum_{j\in A}0\vee\Sigma^*_{ij},\] where $c'$ is a universal constant.

results.notes: Delta in paper is the minimal positive gap (Delta_min). A non-asymptotic bound (eq. rel:fullstate_cov) is given in the appendix proof. Algorithm not efficient for arbitrary action sets.

symbols.s_out: sparsity of realized outcome vectors, ||X||_0 <= s

conditions: n/m, n/s, max(1, s/m) are integers

source.label: thm:lower_sparse
source.quote: For any $n,m,s\in \N^*$ such that $n/m$, $n/s$, $1\vee (s/m)$ are integers, $n/m,n/s\geq 2$, any $\Delta\in (0,\frac{ms}{2(n-m)}]$ and any consistent policy, there is a problem with $n$ arms ... on which the regret satisfies \[\liminf_{T\to \infty} \frac{\Delta }{\log\pa{T}}R_T\geq\frac{s(s\wedge m)\pa{1-2m/\arms}}{4}\]

bound.regime: (Delta (s^m))^{2/3} v (m Delta + m Delta log(Delta_max/Delta)) <= c log(m+1) sum_i nu*_i (s^m)/n

symbols.nu_sum: sum over arms of nu*_i = E|X_i|

conditions: Delta small enough (condition with universal constant c)

source.label: cor:upper_cov
source.quote: Assume that the outcome distribution $\Prb_{\bX}$ satisfies $\Vert{\bold X}\Vert_\infty\leq 1$ and $\Vert{\bold X}\Vert_1\leq s$, and that ... Then the regret of Algorithm~\ref{algo:sparse} is upper bounded as \[\limsup_{T\to \infty} \frac{\Delta}{\log\pa{T}}R_T \leq c' \log^2(m+1) \sum_{i\in [n]}\nu^*_i(s\wedge m)\leq c' \log^2(m+1) (s\wedge m) s,\]

results.notes: Delta is minimal positive gap. Non-asymptotic version in eq. rel:fullstate_sparse.

bound.regime: (Delta (s^m))^{2/3} v (m Delta + m Delta log(Delta_max/Delta)) <= c log(m+1) sum_i nu*_i (s^m)/n

conditions: Delta small enough (condition with universal constant c)
results.notes: Second (simplified) inequality of Corollary 1 using sum nu*_i <= s. Matches Theorem 3 lower bound up to log^2(m+1).
